issue.title: [process] Приёмка: самопроверка автора, выборочная проверка техлида, доработка новым PR в том же issue
issue.body:
## Background

Правила «Приёмки задачи» в `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` хорошие, но всю проверку делает один человек. Если после мержа AC выполнены не целиком, заводят отдельный issue «Хвосты приёмки #N» (17 открытых), исходный закрывают — и задача считается сданной, хотя AC не выполнены. Статус AC Check на доске 12 есть, в документах его нет.

Решение команды:
\- автор сам проводит AC Check (скилл #266, режим «автор»): по каждому AC и DoD — доказательство, комментарий-таблица в issue, статус AC Check;
\- техлид или назначенный принимающий проверяет таблицу выборочно, отмечает чекбоксы и закрывает issue — или возвращает в In Progress со списком;
\- issue не принимается, пока не выполнены все AC и DoD; невыполненное — **новый PR в том же issue** (`Refs #N`), не новый issue;
\- перенос AC в другую задачу — только решением техлида с пометкой у AC; некодовый AC (ruleset, доска, живой прогон) — действие плюс доказательство комментарием;
\- follow-up issue — только для находок вне AC исходной задачи, найденных при приёмке или позже; с исходным issue как родителем;
\- уже открытые «Хвосты приёмки» не переоткрываем и не сливаем — дорабатываются как есть.

## Scope

- `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`: таблица шагов — новый шаг «автор проводит AC Check» между мержем последнего PR и приёмкой; статус AC Check: кто ставит, кто снимает
- `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`, «Приёмка задачи»: самопроверка автора с таблицей «AC → доказательство» обязательна; правило «невыполненный AC — новый PR в том же issue»; перенос AC в другую задачу — только решением техлида с пометкой у AC; некодовый AC — действие плюс доказательство комментарием; follow-up — только вне AC, с родителем; судьба уже открытых «Хвостов приёмки»

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` описывает статус AC Check: ставит автор после самопроверки, снимает принимающий (закрытие → Done или возврат в In Progress)
- [x] В «Приёмке задачи» самопроверка автора с таблицей «AC → доказательство» стоит обязательным шагом перед AC Check; принимающий проверяет таблицу и закрывает
- [x] Явное правило: невыполненный AC или DoD — новый PR с `Refs #N` в том же issue; отдельный issue для этого не заводится
- [x] Записаны исключения: перенос AC в другую задачу — только решением техлида с пометкой у AC; некодовый AC — действие плюс доказательство комментарием
- [x] Follow-up заводится только для нового скоупа, sub-issue исходного; правило про уже открытые «Хвосты приёмки» записано

## Dependencies

**Блокирующие:**

- нет

**Блокирует:**

- #266 — скилл приёмки реализует эти правила

**Связано, не блокирует:**

- #271 — мерж
- #262 — follow-up с родителем
- Порядок мержа #271 → #272 → #273: все три правят одни разделы `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`

## DoD Checklist

- [x] Документы обновлены и не противоречат друг другу
- [x] PR одобрен на текущей голове, все треды закрыты
- [x] Статус на доске 12 обновлён

## References

- https://github.com/larchanka-training/dmc-268-api-t6/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#приёмка-задачи
- Пример текущей практики: #245, #244, #243

## Kickoff — с чего начать

**Репозиторий:** larchanka-training/dmc-268-api-t6

**Ветка:** `docs/<n>-acceptance-by-author` — `main` защищён, через PR с `Refs #<n>`

**Форма проблемы:** Приёмка держится на одном человеке, а «Хвосты приёмки» позволяют закрыть задачу с невыполненными AC. Правка процесса переносит сбор доказательств на автора и запрещает выносить невыполненный AC в новый issue.

**Что прочитать первым:**

- `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` — таблица шагов, «Про доску», «Приёмка задачи»
- #117 — как сейчас выглядит приёмка

**Мины:**

- Шаг «Done ставит workflow Item closed» остаётся: AC Check снимается закрытием issue, а не переносом карточки
- «Назначенный принимающий» уже есть в правилах — не вводить новую роль, а опереться на неё

source.title: feat(agents): add the issue-graph script for sprint dependency graphs
source.body:
## What

Part 1 of api#268: a deterministic script, `.agents/skills/issue-graph/scripts/issue_graph.py`, that builds the dependency graph of a sprint from GitHub native relations. It uses no LLM. The `SKILL.md` and publishing come in part 2.

- **Input**:
  - a milestone, matched by exact title in api and ui;
  - an epic's sub-issues;
  - or a list of `api#N` / `ui#N` / `owner/name#N`.
- **Reads**: `parent`, `blockedBy`, `blocking` and the Status on board 12, through `gh api graphql`. It sends one query per repo with the relations nested, not one query per issue. The scope is paginated by 50, and so are nested `blockedBy`/`blocking` (follow-up `node(id:)` pages).
- **Output**: a Markdown report on stdout.
  - A Mermaid graph. Sub-issues are drawn inside their parent's subgraph. A closed blocker is a dotted edge. Each node has a status class (done / In Progress / On Review·AC Check / alarm / outside the scope).
  - Cycles.
  - In Progress issues that have an open blocker.
  - Parallel layers. Layer 1 is "can be taken now".
  - The critical path.
  - Issues without links.
  - Issues outside the scope.
- **Exit codes**:
  - `0` — report printed;
  - `1` — report printed and the graph has a cycle; layers and critical path are not computed;
  - `2` — input error, including a NOT_FOUND ref or a milestone that is in no repo;
  - `3` — gh / GraphQL failure.
- **Tests**: offline pytest on GraphQL fixtures. They use the `ISSUE_GRAPH_FIXTURE_DIR` seam, and an autouse fake `gh` fails any real call. Six byte-exact golden reports, written by hand before the code: `cycle`, `no-links`, `milestone` (ui + api, container, cross-repo edge, external blocker, tie-break), `epic` (the shape of #139), `pagination`, `issues`. 59 tests.
- **Sync** (api copy: larchanka-training/dmc-268-api-t6#275): `.agents/README.md` lists `skills/issue-graph/**` in the sync map and notes that JSON fixtures carry no marker. Its goldens and fixtures are added to `.prettierignore`.

No new dependency: python3 stdlib only, as in `create-issue`.

`skills/issue-graph/` has no `SKILL.md` until part 2. Harnesses that look for `SKILL.md` skip the directory until then. The script and its tests stand alone.

## Why

The sprint's dependencies are visible only in pieces. blocked-by and sub-issues are set by hand, and the rest lives as text in Dependencies. Team decision in api#273: build the graph once the sprint's issues are filed, and publish it in the sprint epic. This part provides the graph. Publishing and the skill come in part 2.

**Compared with existing skills** (repo heads read 2026-10-24):

- **mattpocock/skills** `wayfinder`/`to-tickets`. Taken: native blockedBy as the source of truth, and the "frontier" rule, which here is layer 1. Not taken: his `Blocked by:` fallback that parses issue text. We read native relations only.
- **addyosmani/agent-skills** `planning-and-task-breakdown`. Not taken: its graph is drawn by hand. Ours comes from data and cannot drift.
- **OpenSpec**, the `add-change-stacking-awareness` proposal. Taken: cycles are reported before layering, and ties have a deterministic tie-break. Not taken: `provides/requires` markers, since GitHub has nothing to hold them.
- None of the three computes a critical path or publishes a graph to GitHub.
- The curator's set promised after the 26.10 call has not been received yet. It will be compared before part 2.

**OpenCode** ([skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/), [rules](https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/), docs dated 2026-10-23) reads `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and `AGENTS.md` (`CLAUDE.md` only when there is no `AGENTS.md`). Our `.claude/skills` is a symlink onto `.agents/skills`, so OpenCode sees every skill twice. Its docs do not say which copy wins. This applies to all skills, not only this one. `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1` turns the `.claude/skills` path off.

## How to verify

```sh
# offline tests (not part of the required CI job — same decision as create-issue)
uv run --no-project --with pytest pytest -p no:cacheprovider .agents/skills/issue-graph/tests
# byte-identity with the api copy (api PR: larchanka-training/dmc-268-api-t6#275)
diff -r ../dmc-268-api-t6/.agents/skills/issue-graph .agents/skills/issue-graph
# live: the board Status needs the read:project scope (default gh login lacks it)
gh auth refresh -s read:project
.agents/skills/issue-graph/scripts/issue_graph.py --epic api#139
.agents/skills/issue-graph/scripts/issue_graph.py --milestone "Спринт 4"
```

ruff (`check` and `format --check`) and `mypy --strict` run against the api copy, because ui has no Python toolchain. The api PR lists the commands. The tests also pass under api's pytest config.

Review before opening: one clean-context review in two rounds. The first round raised no P1. Its P2 findings were gaps in the tests (closed blockers, cursors on the wire, nested pages past p2), and they are closed with mutation checks. Its P3 findings are applied too. One ambiguity was settled: an out-of-scope issue that only waits on an in-scope one renders as `— ждёт <ref>`, with no «блокирует».

Titles outside the Mermaid block get a zero-width space after `#` and `@`, written as `​`. The GitHub markdown API showed that `\#` and `#` still produce issue links and mentions, so `​` is the only one of the three that stops the published report from cross-linking issues or pinging people. Code spans are left untouched.

## Live run: epic api#139

`issue_graph.py --epic api#139`, exit 0, run on 2026-10-24. The report shows the external blockers api#130 and api#219 and the chain 144 → 146 → 147.

source.title: feat(agents): publish the issue graph and add the issue-graph skill
source.body: ## What Part 2 of api#268: publishing and the skill around the part-1 script (ui#177). - **`--publish-to N|REF`** (`issue_graph.py`) — the report also goes to one comment whose first line is `` (`milestone=`, `epic=<repo>#<n>` or `issues=<sorted refs>`). A re-run with the same scope finds that comment (REST listing, 100 per page, oldest first, capped at 100 pages) and PATCHes it; otherwise it POSTs one. A bare `N` is `api#N`, so `--publish-to 261` targets the «Спринт 4» issue. Without `--publish-to` the script makes no REST call and the report is byte-identical to part 1 (goldens unchanged, except `cycle.md` — see review round 1 below). - **Never publishes** a graph with a cycle (report printed, exit 1) or a body over GitHub's 65536-character limit (exit 2). In fixture mode gh is still never called: comment pages come from fixtures and writes go to `ISSUE_GRAPH_WRITE_LOG`, so a fixture run cannot post a fake graph; an empty `ISSUE_GRAPH_FIXTURE_DIR` is an error, not a live run. - **`examples/`** — four golden request/outcome pairs, written before `SKILL.md`: show a sprint graph (live), publish and re-run into the same comment (live), refuse to publish a cycle (fixture), flag In Progress work waiting on an open blocker (fixture). - **`SKILL.md`** (244 lines, one context, no sub-agents) + `references/report.md` (what each section means) + `references/publishing.md` (marker, matching, failures, fixture seam). `AGENTS.md` lists the skill. Commits, one per prompt (`docs/prompts/268/06`–`12`): the script and tests, the examples, `SKILL.md`, two clean-context review rounds (script: 2 P2 test gaps + 6 P3; skill: 3 P2 + 10 P3 — all applied), fixes from the first manual runs, and team review round 1 (`2d81cdb`): - **«Циклы» names the whole cyclic component.** Under a cycle line, one nested line `- в том же клубке связей ещё: …` lists the component's other issues in key order, tagged `(вне выборки)`, `(закрыта)` or both; a component that is just its cycle gets none. The cycle line itself is unchanged; `cycle.md` is the only golden that changed. A graph with a cycle is never published, so the comment format is not affected. - **The marker key escapes CR and LF** (`%0D`, `%0A`, after `%` and before `>`), so a multi-line milestone title still matches its comment on a re-run. Titles without them keep today's marker — the api#261 comment still matches. ## Why api#273 makes the graph part of sprint start: once the sprint's issues are filed, the milestone graph is published to the «Спринт N» issue. Re-runs during the sprint must update that one comment, not pile up new ones, and the agent must not invent links or publish a broken graph. Decisions worth a look: - **The marker is per scope, not per issue**: a milestone graph and an epic graph can live side by side in one issue. The repo set is not part of the key (a `--repo`-narrowed run updates the same comment — `SKILL.md` keeps `--repo` away from `--publish-to`); owner/name are lower-cased. - **No author filter**: a teammate's re-run updates the same comment (write access can edit others' comments). source.body:
## What

Part 1 of #273: sprints are milestones.

**`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`, new `## 9. Спринты`** (appended after §8; §1–§8 are unchanged, so the `#мерж` / `#приёмка-задачи` anchors still resolve; the header row «Задача» gains #273):

- name «Спринт N», identical in both repos; milestones are per repo, so title and due date are edited in both; start date in the description, due date once announced;
- who creates it (tech lead, both repos, by sprint start) and who sets it: whoever files the issue (`create-issue` sets `milestone` from the spec), the tech lead when marking the sprint composition, the author when taking an issue without a milestone into work (§2 step 1);
- an open issue without a milestone is backlog (not the board's Backlog view, which filters by status; sprints 1–3 are not marked);
- the sprint composition rule: open on the start date with an assignee in In Progress / On Review / AC Check, plus Todo by the tech lead's list;
- the «Спринт N» issue as the place for the sprint graph, named by number (for Спринт 4 the process epic #261); sprint issues are not added to it as sub-issues, so the graph is built from the milestone;
- the board 12 view Sprints and two `gh` commands: list a sprint in both repos, set a milestone.

**Done outside the diff** (AC 1 and 3 of part 1):

source.body:
## What

SYNC copy of larchanka-training/dmc-268-ui-t6#213 (Part 1 of #266): `.agents/skills/accept-issue/` byte-identical to the ui branch (`diff -r` empty) — the facts script and its offline tests. Merge after ui#213.

- `closing.events` — **every** `ClosedEvent` and `ReopenedEvent` (paginated, chronological), each with `actor`, `state_reason` and `closer`: `manual` (null), `merge` (PullRequest), `commit`, `project` (ProjectV2); `last_closer` and `ever_closed_by_merge` on top. Classification is by `closer`, never by `actor`.
- `checkboxes.ac` / `checkboxes.dod` — total, checked and item text, counted only under `## Acceptance Criteria` and `## DoD Checklist`; fenced code, blockquotes and HTML comments are skipped; `outside` counts the rest.
- `prs` — every PR from the timeline `CROSS_REFERENCED_EVENT`, from both repos: state, `merged_at`, head SHA, CI rollup, unresolved review threads (paginated past 100), `will_close`, and `refs` — the PR names this issue with `Refs #N` (same repo) or `Refs OWNER/NAME#N` (any repo); a bare `Refs #N` in the other repo does not count.
- Exit 0 / 2 (usage, bad REF) / 3 (gh or API error, not found, bad shape). Read-only: GraphQL queries only.

`SKILL.md`, `examples/`, the `AGENTS.md` list and the `.agents/README.md` sync map and skill count come in Part 2 (after #272). The ui-only `.prettierignore` lines have no api counterpart.

## Why

Acceptance commands 1–3 in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Приёмка задачи") are run by hand by one person, and command 1 only sees the last close. The script collects the mechanical facts in one run so the author can build the AC → evidence table and the acceptor only checks it (api#272).

Prior art: CONTRIBUTING commands 1–3 (now all events instead of `last: 1`) and the offline seam of `issue-graph` (copied, not imported — each skill is self-contained). The comparison with ready-made skills (Matt Pocock, Addy Osmani, OpenSpec) belongs to the `SKILL.md` in Part 2.

source.title: docs(contributing): start acceptance with an author self-check (#272)
source.body:
## What

Process rules for issue acceptance in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (the only file changed):

- New step 8: the issue assignee (the author) self-checks after the last PR is merged and posts an "AC → evidence" table in the issue, then sets AC Check. Old step 8 becomes step 9: the tech lead or the appointed acceptor samples the table, ticks the AC and DoD boxes and accepts the issue, or returns the card to In Progress with a list of what is left.
- Rework stays in the same issue: a code AC is finished by a new PR with `Refs #N`, a non-code AC by an action plus evidence in a comment. No separate issue for it.
- Exceptions: moving an AC to another issue is the tech lead's decision only, noted at the AC; a non-code AC (ruleset, board, live run) is an action plus evidence.
- Follow-ups from acceptance are only for new scope outside the AC, as sub-issues of the original; the open "Хвосты приёмки" issues are finished as they are, new ones are not created.
- The §2 flowchart shows both rework paths: an unmet code AC goes back to a new PR (step 2); a non-code AC, including a task without a PR, goes through an action-plus-evidence node into the self-check (step 8).
- §1 (roles), the board notes ("Про доску"), §7 (agreements table) and §9 (sprint composition) are aligned with the new steps; the step 2 reference to the acceptance step now says step 9.

## Why

Acceptance is done by one person today, and when the AC are only partly met the original issue is finished and a "Хвосты приёмки #N" issue is opened (17 open), so the task counts as delivered with unmet AC. The team decided that the author self-checks first, the tech lead samples, and unmet work stays in the same issue.

## How to verify

- Open the rendered `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` on the branch: the mermaid flowchart in §2 shows steps 8 and 9, the back-edges to the PR step for a code AC and the non-code action node leading into step 8; the §2 table rows 8–9 match it.
- Read "Про доску" and "Приёмка задачи": the AC Check owner (sets / clears), the self-check row, the "Если не всё выполнено" row and the five bullets for rework, AC transfer, non-code AC, follow-ups and open "Хвосты приёмки".
- `git diff --stat origin/main` shows one file; bash commands 1–6 in §2 are untouched.

Known seam (not fixed here): the `implement-issue` preflight stops on a rework PR (a task without parts that already has a PR, every part merged). The rework loop belongs to #269 Part 2; #266 (`accept-issue`) implements these rules.
